traps.shape: the reported sink plus its how-type half: stored credentials are attached to whatever URL the query resolves to, so the destination must be decided from the effective URL before any credential is attached, and the saved path before run-time parameter expansion is the only evidence of the destination the query author actually authored; the shapes are a foreign host, a look-alike host (api.example.com.collector.example.net), a different port, a different scheme, a base address with no scheme, and the same set reached through a caller-supplied parameter; coupled must-keep-working: relative and same-origin absolute paths, a datasource with no base address whose saved path names the host directly (credentialed), a parameterised path that stays on the origin, and a template datasource whose base the runner rewrites
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the report shows a single parameterised path, so an absolute-URL check or a string prefix against the stored base looks sufficient; the saved-path producer sits in the query runner, a layer the integration never calls back into
traps.realistic_because: published fix site (GHSA-MQHR-6J6H-74P5); the parameter shape is the advisory's own public-query vector and the saved-path producer is the published fix's own second edit site

traps.shape: a same-origin request answered with a redirect to another origin; the shared outbound helper strips only four well-known header names, so datasource defaultHeaders (arbitrary names) and an apiKey auth header ride the hop; a fix limited to the initial URL never sees the hop, and a fix that adds more names to the strip list still misses the arbitrary apiKey name; coupled must-keep-working: same-origin redirects keep the credentials, and other helper callers (automation webhooks, plugin downloads, the OAuth2 token endpoint) keep following cross-origin redirects
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the shared helper already deletes Authorization/cookie headers when a redirect changes origin, so the outbound layer reads as already handled and the report is about the REST integration
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: redirect handling predates the advisory and lives in another package; the published fix adds the opt-in there

traps.shape: the stored OAuth2 client credential is sent in the token request body (or a Basic header); a 307/308 from the token endpoint to another origin re-sends the body, so the client secret follows a hop; header stripping does not cover a body, and the REST integration's opt-in does not reach this call site; coupled must-keep-working: normal token acquisition, the header-credentials method, and a same-origin redirect on the token endpoint
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the advisory is about datasource request headers, the token endpoint is a trusted identity provider's URL, and the shared helper's existing header stripping looks like it already covers credentials
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the token request predates the advisory and every published fix commit leaves it unchanged; the credential is a datasource-stored OAuth2 client secret
